title: Consolidated check — v1.0
description: Chainlink #55/#56. The output contract for the future `ligature check --json`, specified here so #56 implements against a fixed shape. Not implemented by this task -- #56 owns the gate-discovery/consolidation engine this document describes the OUTPUT of. `mutated_workspace` is a required const-false field: check is read-only by construction (docs/trust-and-compatibility-boundaries.md), and this schema makes that guarantee machine-checkable rather than a claim only prose makes. Determinism: for two runs over byte-identical workspace contents and an identical installed product, every field in this document EXCEPT `run_metadata` (explicitly excluded, see its own description) must serialize to byte-identical JSON under `scripts/schema_utils.py`-style canonical dumping (sort_keys, fixed separators, trailing newline) -- tests/test_consolidated_check_schema.py checks this canonicalization property directly against fixture documents, not against a real check run (there is no real check run to test yet).

mutated_workspace.description: Always false. check never approves, promotes, edits, or weakens anything -- this field exists so that guarantee is schema-enforced, not merely documented. A future check-adjacent command that DOES write (there is none today) would need its own schema, not a true value smuggled in here.

run_metadata.description: Optional. Wall-clock/host detail (started_at, duration_ms, invoking product version) that is real and useful but NOT part of the determinism guarantee above -- two runs over identical inputs produce different run_metadata by construction (different wall-clock time) while every other field must still match byte-for-byte. Consumers that need byte-identical comparison across runs must exclude this object first.

gates.description: One entry per gate-id in docs/cli-contract.md §3's vocabulary that check considered for this run -- including ones it decided NOT to run. A gate check never considered at all (e.g. one added to the CLI after this run) is simply absent; a gate check considered and not run always has a `skipped`/`blocked` entry with a `reason`.

next_action.description: Exactly zero (null) or one recommended next action -- never an array, never more than one. null means check found nothing actionable to recommend (which is NOT the same as 'clean': see `result.exit_code`, which can still be non-zero with next_action null, e.g. a human decision already recorded and nothing further to automate).

result.description: The exit-code contract (docs/exit-code-contract.md) applied to this run's own findings/gates/next_action -- makes the connection between the JSON body and the process exit code explicit and independently checkable rather than something only the process's own return value asserts.

conditions.description: The condition set scripts/exit_codes.py:resolve() was called with to produce exit_code -- present even when empty (exit_code 0).

reason.description: Required whenever outcome is skipped/not-applicable/blocked (see the conditional below) -- WHY, not just that. e.g. 'no closure profiles present' (not-applicable), 'blocked on extract-c-static: no C_static reports' (blocked).

dedup_key.description: Deterministic identity: a stable digest of (gate_id, subject, reason) or equivalent canonical fields -- the SAME underlying problem reported by two different gate runs (or re-derived on a second identical run) must produce the identical dedup_key, so consolidation can drop duplicates by key equality rather than fuzzy text matching.

subject.description: The artifact path or id this finding is about.

authority.description: What kind of source stands behind this finding -- a mechanized-gate finding is a deterministic, recomputed fact; llm-advisory is a model's suggestion, never authoritative on its own; human-decision-pending names a gap only a human checkpoint can close; external-authority-missing/backend-unavailable name findings that exist because something check needed wasn't reachable, not because a check ran and failed.

provenance.description: Which script/gate/function produced this, e.g. 'scripts/gate_r1_g16.py:gate_r1_g16_workspace'. Not frozen as public API (module names can change) -- this field exists for audit/debugging, not as a contract surface itself.

kind.description: automated-command: check can name the exact next CLI invocation (e.g. `ligature gate g14 --cluster mcmc-chain`) that would make progress. human-decision: no command exists -- a person must decide something first (plan.md §7.2's authority split). external-authority-missing: the next step needs an approval/policy/authority this workspace does not have recorded at all. backend-unavailable: the next step needs an LLM backend or verifier dispatch target that isn't configured or didn't respond.

action_id.description: The STABLE, versioned identifier for what this action does -- required whenever kind is 'automated-command'. THIS is the machine-consumable contract surface, not `command` below (round-3 external review: an earlier revision let `command` be the only identifier offered, while pointing at legacy flat command names docs/cli-contract.md §7 itself declares unversioned and changeable without notice -- a consumer keying off `command` had nothing stable to key off at all). Closed to an `enum` as of v1.0 (round-4 external review: an open pattern let any invented kebab-case string validate, which is not actually a versioned vocabulary -- `refresh-*` for the three internal operations, `author-interaction` for the example in schemas/examples/consolidated-check.blocked.example.json) -- docs/cli-contract.md §7 is this enum's own documentation, not a separate, looser source of truth. Extending this list is an additive, minor schema-version change (new value, nothing removed or renarrowed) exactly like adding an artifact-kind or gate-id elsewhere in this contract; #56 is expected to add more as `check`'s own recommendation logic grows, each one landing here at the same time it lands in docs/cli-contract.md, never before.

command.description: A best-effort LITERAL CLI invocation for human/script convenience only -- explicitly NOT a stability guarantee and NOT something automated tooling may parse or pattern-match (key off `action_id` instead). May be non-null even when it currently names a legacy flat command whose shape carries no compatibility promise (docs/cli-contract.md §7). Required to be present (string or null) on every next_action; required NON-NULL specifically when kind is 'automated-command', unconditionally -- there is no case where an automated-command next_action may omit a literal command, only a case where that literal is not itself a stability guarantee (round-4 external review: an earlier revision of this description claimed command could still become null for an automated-command action, which directly contradicted the conditional two lines below that always requires it non-null; that claim is removed, not the requirement).

change_request_stub.description: A machine-readable pointer toward opening a real change request -- not the request itself. check proposes; it never creates or approves one.
